title: Usage-linked capacity credits and SLA bundles for private deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Overview:
This ticket defines an alternative packaging experiment for Private/VPC and on-prem customers that ties license fees to a mix of a fixed base license plus 'usage-linked capacity credits' and optional SLA bundles. The goal is to create a predictable economic model for enterprise buyers that aligns Redwood revenue with customer scale while preserving a clear upgrade path and compliance controls for security questionnaires.

Problem statement:
Enterprise procurement frequently pushes back on pure node-based or flat per-core pricing for private deployments. Customers want: (1) predictable baseline cost for budgeting, (2) the ability to scale usage with credits to avoid long renegotiations, and (3) clearly scoped SLAs and support add-ons for regulated workloads. Existing offers are either too rigid (strict node-count licensing) or too opaque (ad-hoc discounts and ad-hoc support).

Proposed experiment:
- Pricing components:
  - Base license fee: annual minimum covering the control plane and core runtime support (covers 1 reserve capacity unit).
  - Capacity credits: pre-purchased units that can be consumed by throughput (tokens / vCPU-hour-equivalent / inference units). Credits can be top-ups or committed monthly/annual bundles.
  - SLA bundles: Bronze (24x5 email), Silver (24x7 email + 8hr critical), Gold (24x7 + 4hr critical + platform health checks), Platinum (Gold + dedicated success contact + quarterly on-site review).
  - Optional add-ons: compliance package (audit log retention >13 months, KMS integration assisted onboarding), accelerated upgrade window (guaranteed security patch within 7 days).

Hypothesis:
- Moving to usage-linked credits reduces procurement friction for customers with variable workloads and increases Average Contract Value (ACV) through bundled SLAs and committed credit discounts.
- Sales cycles shorten when there is a simple base + credits framing vs complex node entitlement tables.

Success metrics:
- Pilot conversion rate: >= 30% of targeted enterprise accounts accept the credits model within Q2 pilot.
- ACV uplift: +15% net ARR for pilot cohort vs baseline.
- Time-to-sign: reduce median procurement time by 20%.
- Security questionnaire pass-rate remains >= 95% after packaging changes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Pricing page and one-pager for sales updated and approved by Finance and Legal.
- Contract language drafted covering credit consumption, rollover policy, refunds, and upgrade/downgrade mechanics.
- Security questionnaire mapping updated to include how credits and SLAs map to logs/KMS/upgrade windows.
- Pilot offer ready with at least two reference configurations (SMB-committed credits + Bronze SLA; Enterprise-annual credits + Gold SLA + Compliance package).

Implementation notes for PM/Eng collaboration:
- Billing integration: define how credits decrement against consumption metrics (token-based or inference-unit-based), and how overages are handled.
- Metering signals: align with runtime teams to ensure reliable counters (per-tenant KPIs), and retention policies for auditing consumption.
- Upgrade cadence options: document three upgrade tracks for Private deployments - Standard (quarterly non-disruptive), Accelerated (monthly security patches with scheduled slots), and Hotfix (emergency patches within 7 days for Platinum customers).
- Sales tooling: quote generator templates (Sheets + Salesforce config) that accept base fee, credit bundle, and SLA to produce ACV and monthly charge.

Security questionnaire and contract considerations:
- Add explicit language in contract Addendum A for upgrade windows and emergency patch obligations when customers opt into Accelerated/Hotfix tracks.
- For compliance package buyers, include explicit evidence artifacts we can provide (audit logs export, KMS key rotation notes, and SOC2 attestation references).
- Prepare standard responses to top 20 security questionnaire items that enterprise buyers ask when adopting private deployments (e.g., data residency, encryption in transit/at rest, KMS handling, access controls).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Customers may prefer unlimited on-prem usage and balk at credits. Mitigation: Offer high-volume committed bundles with built-in discounts and a 10% rollover for unused credits.
- Risk: Metering disputes. Mitigation: Provide transparent per-tenant consumption dashboards and signed measurement definitions in contract.
- Risk: Legal pushback on upgrade SLAs in air-gapped environments. Mitigation: Create a non-intrusive security patch plan and an on-site engineering option in Platinum bundle.

Next steps:
1) Hold discovery workshop with Sales and top 10 enterprise prospects to validate appetite (target by 2025-02-28).
2) Draft contract addendum and security Q&A responses (Legal/Security by 2025-03-10).
3) Implement quote generator and meter mapping for credits (Engineering + Billing, spike complete by 2025-03-21).
4) Launch 8-week pilot with 6 enterprise accounts, measure success criteria, and iterate on terms.
